summary: Under the ECOWAS free movement protocol, a Community citizen visiting for up to 90 days enters free of visa requirements, and the official eVisa portal offers no visa for citizens of Bahamas, Barbados, Botswana, Eswatini, Fiji, Jamaica, Kenya, Lesotho, Malawi, Malaysia, Mauritius, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Singapore, Sri Lanka and Trinidad and Tobago, and for such a nationality it shows "Your nationality has a Visa free benefit, there is no Visa required". Other nationalities can apply on the official eVisa portal (evisa.sl) — USD 80 single entry, USD 25 for African Union nationals — and the visa is issued on arrival at the airport or border once the application is approved. The UK government says British visitors can also get a visa on arrival for USD 80, paid in cash in US dollars.

tips.text: The UK Foreign Office says the visa on arrival costs USD 80, paid in cash in US dollars, or you can apply online for an e-visa before you travel.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Sierra Leone?
faq.answer: ECOWAS citizens visiting for up to 90 days enter free of visa requirements under the ECOWAS free movement protocol, and the official eVisa portal offers no visa for citizens of Bahamas, Barbados, Botswana, Eswatini, Fiji, Jamaica, Kenya, Lesotho, Malawi, Malaysia, Mauritius, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Singapore, Sri Lanka and Trinidad and Tobago, and for such a nationality it shows "Your nationality has a Visa free benefit, there is no Visa required". Other nationalities can apply on the official eVisa portal, evisa.sl (USD 80 single entry; USD 25 for African Union nationals), and the visa is issued on arrival at the airport or border once approved; the UK government says British visitors can also get a visa on arrival for USD 80, paid in cash in US dollars.

faq.question: How much is the Sierra Leone visa on arrival?
faq.answer: The UK Foreign Office says USD 80, paid in cash in US dollars. African Union nationals pay USD 25 for the e-Visa on evisa.sl; no official source we could read says whether that reduced rate also applies at the border. For citizens of Botswana, Eswatini, Kenya, Lesotho, Malawi and Mauritius the eVisa portal offers no visa and shows that no visa is required.

faq.question: Does Sierra Leone have an eVisa?
faq.answer: Yes — the Government of Sierra Leone eVisa Application System at evisa.sl takes applications online and displays the cost once you select your nationality; the portal says an approved visa is issued on arrival at the airport or border.

faq.question: Is yellow fever vaccination required for Sierra Leone?
faq.answer: The UK Foreign Office tells people travelling on a full British citizen passport that they must have a certificate proving yellow fever vaccination to enter Sierra Leone.

faq.question: Is Sierra Leone safe to visit?
faq.answer: The UK Foreign Office says the political situation has improved since the civil war ended in 2002, but it can change and protests can turn violent, so avoid political gatherings and follow any curfews. It says that in a small number of incidents British nationals have been robbed, sometimes at knifepoint, in areas of Freetown such as Congo Cross, Wilkinson Road, Lumley Beach and Aberdeen and at beach resorts along the Freetown peninsula, and that serious traffic accidents are common.
